faqModal.description: These FAQs relate exclusively to the user section of the Kulturkataster, covering topics such as accounts, role and permission management (administrative rights), managing institutions, and editorial workflows (e.g., creating and maintaining profiles). General questions about the mission and benefits of the Kulturkataster, the scope of the different versions, and the methodological approach can be found in the “Info & Services” section of the Kulturkataster. The FAQs are constantly being updated; if your question is not yet listed here, please feel free to email the editorial team at info@kulturkataster.berlin.

bodySections: **In a growing metropolis like Berlin, spaces for art and culture are scarce resources. Displacement, competition for spaces and location are a threat to the cultural spaces in Berlin, which play a diverse and critical role for the city. They are a location factor, tourism magnet and motor for innovation, they serve the transfer of knowledge, have a memorial function and support community by forming a framework for identity for a diverse and inclusive civic society. The Kulturkataster, an inventory of Berlin’s cultural landscape on a digital map that is freely accessible online, is a decisive step in the direction of sustainable cultural urban development.**

The Kulturkataster was mentioned in the guidelines of the governmental policy the current legislative period. At the end of 2022, Kulturraum Berlin gGmbH (KRB) was entrusted with the conceptualization by Berlin’s Senate Department for Culture and Community and presented the starting situation and needs as well as a realization concept for the Kulturkataster in two concept papers (realized by the Studio für unendliche Möglichkeiten). The realization in 2024 was also assigned to KRB. KRB, in turn, tasked Technologiestiftung Berlin with the development of the online-based map application.
## The framework for the development of the Kulturkataster is formed by four cultural policy guidelines that KRB has elaborated with Berlin’s Senate Department for Culture and Community:

1. Evidence-based cultural policy and cultural urban development: The Berlin Kulturkataster creates a comprehensive data basis about cultural spaces in order to allow the creation of fact-based cultural policy and targeted urban development.
2. The protection as well as new development of spaces for culture: The Kulturkataster serves as an instrument for a sustainable monitoring of cultural areas in order to support their preservation and to develop new spaces.
3. The fair distribution of cultural offerings throughout the city and equal opportunities in terms of participation: The Kulturkataster visualizes gaps in cultural offerings and supports urban planning in creating balanced and fair cultural offerings for all Berliners.
4. The improvement of the cooperation between departments, levels and sectors: As a flexible digital planning instrument, the Kulturkataster strengthens the cooperation between the different areas of responsibility, departmental levels as well as Berlin’s entire cultural community.

The Berlin Kulturkataster has been created to create a record of a cultural landscape that is more diverse, dynamic and interdisciplinary than any other. As much as the editorial team wishes that this was not the case, this process can never be completed. This is why a stated goal of the project is to continuously approximate a current state of Berlin’s cultural landscape on the digital map. This can only be achieved in cooperation with those for whom the Kulturkataster can be an important tool – the administrators on the district and state levels in  Berlin, the numerous advocacy groups for the artistic disciplines, academics, experts, activists and, of course, the cultural locations themselves.

A broad idea of the term culture and a descriptive understanding of culture form the foundations of the Kulturkataster. The database has registered a large number of locations. Additional categories and cultural locations will follow in the next versions. Instead of assessing cultural forms of expression, these are described and sorted in the Kulturkataster according to numerous criteria. This values the individual contributions that both the individual locations as well entire disciplines contribute to the cultural framework of the city.

The development of Berlin’s Kulturkataster takes place as a learning process. This means that new versions of the Kulturkataster will be published at fixed intervals. The future versions are intended to make new functionalities and updated information available. This process allows the project team to integrate suggestions and criticism into the ongoing development process and invites the users of the Kulturkataster to actively participate in its future orientation.

barriers.description: The website currently (as of September 2025) does not offer any content in plain language or videos in German Sign Language (DGS).
barriers.measures: Texts in plain language and explanatory videos in German Sign Language (DGS) are currently in progress.
barriers.timeline: The content is scheduled to be published in plain language and DGS in October 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: Content

barriers.description: The cultural locations in the cultural cadastre are currently only displayed via an interactive map view.
barriers.measures: It is planned to provide a supplementary list view of cultural locations that is fully keyboard and screen reader friendly.
barriers.timeline: The list view is expected to be implemented by December 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: View

barriers.description: Some of the documents provided on the website, such as:
barriers.measures: In the future, the documents will be offered in a barrier-free form.
barriers.timeline: The revision of the existing files is planned for 2026.
barriers.title: Barrier: documents

barriers.description: Some interactive elements of the website - in particular filter functions, map elements or navigation points - cannot currently be operated via keyboard.
barriers.measures: The technical structure of the website is being revised to ensure full keyboard control of all interactive elements.
barriers.timeline: Implementation will take place by the end of 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: Keyboard operability

barriers.description: When navigating with the keyboard, the visible focus is not clearly visible on all interactive elements.
barriers.measures: The visual focus design is overhauled so that interactive elements are clearly highlighted as you scroll through.
barriers.timeline: Implementation will take place by the end of 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: Visible focus

barriers.description: Some icons or buttons on the website do not have meaningful alternative text.
barriers.measures: All graphic elements are checked and provided with correct alternative texts.
barriers.title: Barrier: Alternative texts for images and symbols

barriers.description: The semantic structure of the website is not fully defined by ARIA roles and landmarks.
barriers.measures: The page structure is supplemented with semantic HTML elements and ARIA roles to improve orientation for assistive technologies.
barriers.timeline: Implementation will take place by the end of 2025.
barriers.title: Barrier: Missing ARIA roles and landmarks

barriers.description: The hierarchical structure of the headings is not implemented correctly on all pages.
barriers.measures: The HTML structure is revised to ensure a consistent and logical heading structure.
barriers.timeline: The correction will take place during 2026.
barriers.title: Barrier: Unstructured headings (h1–h6)

barriers.measures: The interactions are technically checked and supplemented to provide feedback to screen readers.
barriers.title: Barrier: Lack of feedback during interactions

downloadModal.dataUseAgreementText: I will not share the data with third parties and will use it exclusively within the limits of legal requirements, in particular the GDPR where personal data is concerned, and only for the purposes of the Kulturkataster. The purposes of the Kulturkataster are non-commercial and comprise the systematic collection, structuring and public provision of data about places of cultural production and use in the State of Berlin, in order to create a reliable data basis for cultural policy decisions, cultural urban development, and collaboration between cultural actors, administration, academia and the public.

accordion.answer: The editorial team aims to show all Berlin cultural locations on the map. This is an ongoing process. Some categories and individual places have not yet been fully recorded. If you are missing a location, you can submit it via the contribution form.
accordion.question: Why is my cultural location not listed in the Kulturkataster?

accordion.answer: You can add or correct information about existing cultural locations and suggest new locations for inclusion. This is possible with guest access or with your own account. All submitted information is reviewed by the editorial team before publication.
accordion.question: How can I add or correct information about a cultural location?

accordion.answer: Entries in the Kulturkataster are not published automatically. The editorial team reviews every entry individually. This can take some time, and we may contact you by email if we have questions.
accordion.question: I submitted my cultural location, but it still does not appear on the map. What is happening?

accordion.answer: The Kulturkataster grows with every version. The project team started with a small selection of specialist maps from the Geoportal and will add further maps based on user feedback. You can send suggestions to [info@kulturkataster.berlin](mailto:info@kulturkataster.berlin).
accordion.question: Why does the Kulturkataster include only a few specialist maps from the Geoportal?

accordion.answer: This version does not yet offer independent data management. If you want your venue removed, please contact the editorial team at [info@kulturkataster.berlin](mailto:info@kulturkataster.berlin).
accordion.question: How can I have my cultural location removed from the Kulturkataster?

accordion.answer: In principle, interested people aged 18 or older can create an account in the Kulturkataster.
accordion.question: Who can create an account and which account types are available?

accordion.answer: After registering, you will receive an email to confirm your email address. Once confirmed, your account is active. If you state that you work for a Berlin district, the State of Berlin, a network, or an association, the editorial team will review this information before assigning the relevant access and contribution rights.
accordion.question: When will my account be activated?

accordion.answer: When logged in, you will find the “My cultural locations” section in the Kulturkataster portal. You can suggest a new cultural location or request that an existing location be assigned to your account. After assignment, it appears in your personal overview and you can suggest changes or additions.
accordion.question: How can I add a new cultural location or assign an existing location to my account?

accordion.answer: All data submitted through a user account or guest access is reviewed by the Kulturkataster editorial team before publication. This applies to new venues as well as changes or additions to existing entries.
accordion.question: When and how is data I entered published?

accordion.answer: If you forgot your password, click “Forgot password” in the login area. You will receive an email with a link to set a new password. If you are already logged in, you can change your password in the Kulturkataster portal settings.
accordion.question: What can I do if I forgot my password or want to change it?

accordion.answer: You can download a list of cultural locations using the downward arrow in the navigation. Before downloading, you must confirm that you have read and agree to the data-use agreements and legal notices.
accordion.question: What are the requirements for receiving an account as an administration employee or as an employee of a network or association?

accordion.answer: You can download a list of cultural locations using the downward arrow in the navigation. Before downloading, you can filter or sort the data shown on the map. The export is available in XLS, XLSX, or CSV format. The downloaded data corresponds to the visible data state and your access rights.
accordion.question: How does the data download work?

infoModal.body:
**Since September 2025, the Kulturkataster Berlin has provided the first version of our digital tool for systematically recording Berlin's cultural landscape.**

The Kulturkataster continues to grow: version 2 is planned for early 2026, and version 3 will follow in mid-2026. With every new version, we add more cultural venues, enrich the information, and add new features.\
You can help us. Use this [link](/institution) to submit missing cultural venues and suggest changes.\
**For suggestions and feedback, contact us at:** [info@kulturkataster.berlin](mailto:info@kulturkataster.berlin)\
The current version of the Kulturkataster is version 1.

infoModal.tab1:
## Scope version 1
**Published November 2025**
- {{count}} cultural venues with basic information (name, full address, general contact information, funding and financing information)
- 15 categories and 71 subcategories
- Integration of 12 specialist maps from Geoportal Berlin
- A search field for addresses and names of cultural venues
- A search filter for district, category, and subcategory. Closed cultural venues can also be displayed.

**The following extensions for version 1 were added by November 2025**
- Information in German Sign Language
- Information in plain language
- Accessible list view
infoModal.tab2:
## How to use

The Kulturkataster Berlin is designed to be as intuitive as possible. Its functions follow common map applications. We have summarized the basic controls here.

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/1_Bewegen.jpg|left|Move the map|On a computer: hold the left mouse button and drag the map in the desired direction.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: touch the screen with one finger and swipe across the map.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/2_Zoom.jpg|right|Zoom|On a computer: use the mouse wheel or the plus and minus buttons at the bottom right of the screen.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: place two fingers on the screen and move them apart to zoom in. Move them together to zoom out.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/3_Suche.jpg|left|Search for a venue|On a computer: open the search field with the magnifying glass icon at the top left.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: open the search field with the magnifying glass icon at the bottom. Enter the name of a venue or an address and confirm your search.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/4_Filter.jpg|right|Use filters|You can filter cultural venues by district and by assigned categories and subcategories.\nOn a computer: open the filter with the icon showing three stacked lines at the top left.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: tap the icon with three stacked lines at the top left.\nBy default, all open cultural venues are shown on the map. Use “Show closed venues” to also display temporarily or permanently closed cultural venues.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/5_Download.jpg|left|Download a selection|The Kulturkataster lets you download information about individual cultural venues or all venues in your current view.\nOn a computer: click the downward arrow in the side navigation at the top left.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: tap the downward arrow in the navigation at the bottom right.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/6_Mitwirken.jpg|right|Submit a venue|On a computer: open the contribution form with the pencil icon at the top left.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: open the contribution form with the pencil icon at the bottom right.\nFollow the form instructions and fill in the data fields carefully. Required fields are marked with an asterisk.\nConfirm the consent statement and submit the form.\nThe editorial team will review your entry and contact you by email if there are questions.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/7_Schrift.jpg|left|Change font size|On a computer: open the accessibility menu with the person icon at the bottom left.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: open the menu at the top right and then select the button with the person icon.\nSelect “Change font size”.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/8_Kontrast.jpg|right|Adjust contrast|On a computer: open the accessibility menu with the person icon at the bottom left.\nOn a smartphone/tablet: open the menu at the top right and then select the button with the person icon.\nSelect “Adjust contrast”.`

welcomeModal.description1: The Kulturkataster is a digital map that depicts the diversity of Berlin’s cultural landscape and that systemically registers locations for art and culture. It serves as the central basis for a fact-based approach to cultural urban development. Alongside the public participation function, the new portal with log-in functionality now provides a genuine tool for the practice of collaboratively managing locations.
welcomeModal.description2: Strengthen this project for Berlin’s culture together with us! We look forward to your support.
